Saudi Standards, Metrology and Quality Organization (SASO)

Technical Regulation for Electric Vehicles

The update of this technical regulation was approved at the meeting of the SASO Board of

Directors No. (202), held on (03/10/2024).

The update was published in the Official Gazette on

(03/01/2025).

Version 3

Preamble In line with the accession of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) to the World Trade Organization (WTO), as per the Council of Ministers' Decree No. 244, dated 21/09/1426 A.H.,approvingthe documentation on the Kingdom’s accession tothe WTO, and the requirements for aligning the Kingdom’s relevant regulations with the principles of WTO agreements, particularly the Technical Barriers to Trade (TBT) Agreement, which stipulates that no unnecessary technical requirements shall hinder the flow of goods among member states and that technical requirements and conformity assessment methods shall not discriminate between products based on origin,through theissuance of technical regulations that includeessential legitimate requirements and standardized business procedures. In accordance with Article 3 (Clause-1) of the Statute of the Saudi Standards, Metrology, and Quality Organization (SASO), issued by the Council of Ministers’ Decree No. 216, dated 17/06/1431 A.H. (31/05/2010 A.D.), stipulating that: “SASO shall issue Saudi standards, quality systems, and conformity assessment guidelines, in alignment with international standards and guidelines, ensuring compliance with the requirements of the World Trade Organization (WTO) Agreement, while adhering toIslamic Sharia and serving the interests of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.” In accordance with Article 4 (Clause-2) of the Statute of SASO, issued by the Council of Ministers’ Decree No. 216, dated 17/06/1431 A.H. (31/05/2010 A.D.), stipulating that: “SASO shall issue regulations for conformity assessment procedures of goods, products, and services in accordance with the approved standards.” In accordance with Article 4 (Clause-14) of the Statute of SASO, issued by the Council of Ministers’ Decree No. 216, dated 17/06/1431 A.H. (31/05/2010 A.D.), stipulating that: “SASO shall review and develop laws and regulatory provisions related to its areas of work, propose necessary amendments to align with quality and safety requirements, and refer them to the competent authorities for review and issuance in accordance with applicable procedures.” In accordance with Article 6 (Clause-1) of the Statute of SASO, issued by the Council of Ministers’ Decree No. 216, dated 17/06/1431 A.H. (31/05/2010 A.D.), stipulating that: “Subject to Article 4 of this Statute, SASO shall be the national authority responsible for matters related to standards, conformity assessment procedures, granting the quality mark, metrology, and calibration. All public and private sectors shall comply with Saudi standards in all their procurements and operations.” Since the standards of the products covered under a regulation serve as the basis for their conformity with the essential safety requirements outlined in the specified regulation, SASO has developed this Technical Regulation. Note: This preamble and all annexes of this regulation shall form an integral part thereof. [Signature] 3 Saudi Standards www.saso.gov.sa

Article (1): Terms and Definitions 1/1 When applying the provisions of this regulation, the following terms and expressions shall have the meanings indicated beside them, unless the context requires otherwise:

  • Kingdom (KSA):The Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

  • SASO:Saudi Standards, Metrology, and Quality Organization.

  • The Board:SASO's Board of Directors.

  • Regulatory Authorities:Governmental body/bodies with regulatory tasks according to their specializations,

responsible for implementing or monitoring the implementation of technical regulations, whether at customs ports, markets, or manufactories.

  • Technical Regulation:A document approved by the Board that specifies the characteristics of products,

associated processes, and production methods, including applicable administrative provisions that must be complied with. It may also include or specifically address terms, definitions, packaging, and requirements for markings or labeling of products, services, processes, or production methods.

  • Standard:A document approved by the Board that establishes, for regular and recurring use, non-mandatory

rules, instructions, or specifications for products, processes, and production methods. It may also include or specifically address terms, definitions, packaging, and requirements for markings or labeling applicable to products, services, processes, or production methods.

  • Essential Requirements:The specific requirements for products that may affect safety, health, and the

environment, which must be adhered to.

  • Market Surveillance Authorities:Governmental body/bodies responsible for conducting market surveillance

operations.

  • Market Surveillance:Activities and measures taken by the market surveillance authorities to verify that

products comply with the requirements set out in relevant technical regulations and do not pose a risk to health, safety, the environment, or any other aspect related to the protection of public interest.

  • Hazard(s):A potential source of danger.

  • Risk(s):A potential occurrence of harm, associated with the severity of damage.

  • Supplier:Refers to:

o The product manufacturer, if residing in the Kingdom, or any person who presents themselves as the manufacturer of the product by associating their name with the product, a relevant commercial description, or any person who renews the product. o The manufacturer’s agent in the Kingdom if the manufacturer is based outside the Kingdom, or the importer in the absence of a manufacturer’s agent in the Kingdom. o Any person in the supply chain whose activities may affect the characteristics of the product.

  • Conformity Assessment Procedures:A document approved by the Board that outlines the procedures used,

either directly or indirectly, for conformity assessment. [Signature]

4 Saudi Standards www.saso.gov.sa

Continuation of Article (1): Terms and Definitions

  • Notified (Approved) Bodies:Conformity assessment bodies accepted by SASO in accordance with the

Regulation of Conformity Assessment Bodies Acceptance.

  • Certificate of Conformity:A certificate issued by SASO or an approved body, confirming that a product or a

batch thereof complies with the relevant standard requirements.

  • Supplier Declaration of Conformity:A declaration by the supplier stating that their product complies with

applicable legislative requirements without mandatory third-party intervention—neither in the design stage nor in the production stage of the manufacturing process. The declaration may be based on product testing in accordance with the relevant legislation.

  • Certificate of Registration:A certificate issued by SASO in accordance with the applicable registration

procedures, assigned to each unit of electric vehicles upon obtaining the Certificate of Conformity, in accordance with the required conformity assessment procedures listed in this regulation.

  • Placing on the Market:The act of making a product available in the Saudi market, for which either the

manufacturer or the importer is responsible.

  • Making Available on the Market:Any supply of a product for distribution, consumption, or use in the Kingdom

as part of a commercial activity, whether for monetary compensation or free of charge.

  • Withdrawal:Any procedure aimed at preventing a product from being made available on the market or within

the supply chain.

  • Recall:Any procedure aimed at retrieving products already made available to the end user, in accordance with

the recall regulation.

  • Product:Anelectric vehicle, also referred to as anelectric drive vehicle, powered by one or more electric
motors or traction motors for propulsion. Electric vehicles may include Battery Electric Vehicles (BEV) or Plug-
in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEV) .

  • Manufacturer:The entity that holds technical responsibility for manufacturing the vehicle and its spare parts.

  • Supply Chain:All stages that a product undergoes after its manufacturing until it reaches the consumer,

including packaging, wrapping, supplying, transporting, storing, delivering, wholesaling, retailing, and any other related operations.

  • Rechargeable Energy Storage System (REESS):The system responsible for supplying electric power to the

vehicle.

  • Battery Electric Vehicle (BEV):A fully electric vehicle that operates solely on battery power, also known as a
fully electric vehicle . This type of electric vehicle (EV) uses stored chemical energy in rechargeable battery
packs. BEVs rely on electric motors and motor controllers instead of internal combustion engines ( ICEs ) for
propulsion.
  • Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicle (PHEV):A hybrid vehicle equipped with an internal combustion engine and an

electric motor that can be recharged by plugging into an external power source, as well as by its internal engine. Extended-Range Electric Vehicles (EREV)are a subcategory ofPHEVs, where the electric motor is primarily used for propulsion, and the internal combustion engine serves as an additional power source when needed.

  • Direct Contact:The physical contact of individuals with live high-voltage parts.

[Signature] 5 Saudi Standards www.saso.gov.sa

Continuation of Article (1): Terms and Definitions

  • Conductive Connection:Refers to the connection using conductors to an external power source during the

charging of the Rechargeable Energy Storage System (REESS).

  • Electrical Chassis:A set of conductive parts electrically interconnected, with their potential considered as a

reference voltage.

  • External Electric Power Supply:An electric power source operating on alternating current (AC) or direct current

(DC) from outside the vehicle.

  • Live Parts:Conductive parts intended to be electrically energized under normal operating conditions.

  • Service Disconnect:A device used to disconnect the electrical circuit during testing and maintenance of the

Rechargeable Energy Storage System (REESS).

  • Electrical Circuit:A collection of interconnected live parts designed to be electrically powered during normal

operation.

  • Passenger Compartment:The space designated for accommodating passengers, enclosed by the roof, floor, side

walls, doors, exterior glass, front and rear walls or tailgate, as well as electrical protection barriers and enclosures that provide protection against direct contact with high-voltage live parts.

  • Enclosure:A component that surrounds internal units and provides protection against any direct contact.

  • Electric Power Train:The electrical circuit that includes one or more traction motors and may also include a

Rechargeable Energy Storage System (REESS), an electric power conversion system, electronic converters, associated wiring and connectors, and the coupling system for charging the REESS.

  • Electrical Protection Barrier:A component that provides protection against direct contact with high-voltage live

parts.

  • Protection Degree (IPXXB):Protection against contact with high-voltage live parts using an electrical protection

barrier or an enclosure, tested using an articulated test finger (IPXXB).

  • Protection Degree (IPXXD):Protection against contact with high-voltage live parts using electrical protection

barriers or an enclosure, tested using a test wire (IPXXD).

  • Indirect Contact:Contact of individuals with exposed conductive parts.

  • High Voltage:Refers to the classification of an electrical component or circuit when its operating voltage exceeds

60V and reaches up to 1500V DC, or exceeds 30V and reaches up to 1000V AC (root mean square).

  • Specific Voltage Condition:Defined as a condition where the maximum voltage of the electrically connected

circuit does not exceed30V AC (root mean square)between the direct current part and any other live part. [Signature]

6 Saudi Standards www.saso.gov.sa

Continuation of Article (1): Terms and Definitions

  • 60V DC:This condition applies to circuits where the voltage between any two points does not exceed30V ACor

60V DC.

  • Note:When a live part connected to DC power from such an electrical circuit is connected to the chassis and the
specific voltage condition applies, the maximum voltage between any connected part and the electrical chassis
shall be ≤ 30V AC (root mean square) or 60V DC .
  • Electric Vehicle Charging System:A system composed of components that supply the vehicle with direct

current (DC output) and alternating current (AC) for the purpose of recharging the electric vehicle's batteries.

  • Electric Vehicle Connector:A device that establishes an electrical connection with the electric vehicle by

plugging it into theelectric vehicle charging inlet, allowing power to be supplied from an external power source.

  • Electric Vehicle Coupler:The connection between theelectric vehicle charging inletand its respective

connector cablein the electric vehicle.

  • Electric Vehicle Inlet:A device installed on the electric vehicle where theelectric vehicle connectoris plugged
in to transfer electrical power from an external source. The charging inlet is considered part of the electric
vehicle and not part of the electricity supply equipment .
  • Electric Vehicle Storage Battery:A battery consisting of one or more rechargeable electrochemical cells that do

not have provisions for releasing excess gas pressure during normal charging and operation, adding water or electrolyte, or externally measuring the electrolyte's specific gravity.

  • Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment:Equipment composed of conductors, includinggrounded and

ungrounded connectors,electric vehicle connectors,attachment plugs, and all other necessary devices, power outlets, or apparatus designed specifically for transmitting power to an electric vehicle.

  • Electric Vehicle Supply Equipment System:Electrical power supply components that providealternating

current (AC)for the onboard vehicle charger.

  • Personnel Protection System:A system composed of protective means to safeguard individuals from electric

shocks.

  • Grounded Connectors:Vehicle body-mounted connections used for discharging electric charges.

  • Category M Vehicles:Motor vehicles with at least four wheels, designed and manufactured for passenger

transport. This category includes the following subcategories:
o Category M1: Vehicles designed and built for passenger transport, with no more than eight passenger
seats in addition to the driver’s seat.
o Category M2: Vehicles designed and manufactured for passenger transport, with more than eight seats in
addition to the driver’s seat, and with a maximum mass exceeding 3.5 tons but not exceeding 5 tons .
[Signature]
7 Saudi Standards
www.saso.gov.sa

Continuation of Article (1): Terms and Definitions

  • Category M3:Vehicles designed and manufactured for passenger transport, consisting ofmore than eight seats

in addition to the driver’s seat, with a maximum mass exceeding5 tons.

  • Category N Vehicles:Motor vehicles with at least four wheels, designed and manufactured for the transport of

goods. o Category N1:Vehicles designed and manufactured forgoods transport, with a maximum mass not exceeding

  • 5 tons.
o Category N2: Vehicles designed and manufactured for goods transport , with a maximum mass exceeding 3.5
tons but not exceeding 12 tons .
o Category N3: Vehicles designed and manufactured for goods transport , with a maximum mass exceeding 12
tons .
2/1 Any other words and expressions used in this Technical Regulation shall have the meanings specified in the
applicable laws, regulations, and decisions issued by SASO .
[Signature]
8 Saudi Standards
www.saso.gov.sa
Article (2): Scope
This Technical Regulation applies to electric vehicles of categories M and N , with a design speed exceeding 25 km/h ,
in accordance with the definitions and terms stated in Article (1) and the standards specified in Annex (1) .
Article (3): Objectives
This Regulation aims to establish the essential requirements for electric vehicles covered under its scope, along with
the conformity assessment procedures that suppliers must comply with. This ensures that these products meet the
essential requirements aimed at protecting the environment, safeguarding the health and safety of consumers and
road users, and facilitating market surveillance procedures .
Article (4): Obligations of the Supplier

4/1 Technical Requirements

To comply with the requirements of this Regulation , the supplier must meet the essential characteristics of electric
vehicles , as follows:
  • 4/1/1Theelectric vehiclessupplied must meet thetechnical requirementsspecified in thestandards listed

in Annex (1)of thisRegulation. In the absence of Saudi or Gulf standards, international standards shall be applied.

  • 4/1/2Theelectric vehiclesmust be compatible with at leastone of the electric charging system connectors

specified inAnnex (3).

  • 4/1/3Theelectric vehiclessupplied must pass theconformity assessment proceduresstated in this
Regulation , and must be accompanied by a technical file containing all the documents and information
proving the product's conformity with the Regulation's requirements .
  • 4/1/4AMaterial Safety Data Sheet (MSDS)for thebatterymust be attached to theelectric vehicle.

4/2 Essential Requirements

To comply with the requirements of this Regulation , the supplier must fulfill the essential requirements for electric
vehicles , as specified in Annex (2) of this Regulation .

4/3 Metrological (Measurement) Requirements

The International System of Units (SI units) , its multiples, or its sub-units shall be used during the design,
manufacturing, or distribution processes.
9 Saudi Standards
www.saso.gov.sa

4/4 Administrative Requirements

Electric vehicles must comply with the Traffic Regulations and their Implementing Regulations applicable in Saudi
Arabia .
[Signature]
10 Saudi Standards
www.saso.gov.sa

Article (5): Conformity Assessment Procedures

  • 5/1The supplier—responsible for placing and displaying electric vehicles covered under thisRegulationin the
market — must obtain a Type 1a Certificate of Conformity issued by SASO or its authorized body, in
accordance with the General Conformity Assessment Models Regulation issued by SASO .
  • 5/2The product must be accompanied by atechnical filethat includes the following:
o A) Supplier (manufacturer/importer) Declaration of Conformity , in accordance with the model attached
in Annex (4) .
o B) Risk Assessment Document .
o C) Designs and drawings proving the product’s conformity with the requirements of this Regulation .
o D) Necessary warnings and alerts , along with operational manuals for the safe and proper use of the
product.
Article (6): Responsibilities of Regulatory Authorities
Regulatory Authorities, within their competencies and powers, shall undertake the following:
  • 6/1Ensure thatelectric vehiclescovered under thisRegulationcomply with theconformity assessment

proceduresspecified and that the relevanttechnical documentsare attached to the consignments.

  • 6/2Randomlywithdraw samplesofelectric vehiclesand refer them tospecialized laboratoriesto verify their

conformity with therequirementsof thisTechnical Regulation.

  • 6/3Regulatory Authorities have the right tocharge suppliers(manufacturers/importers) for thecosts of tests

and related fees.

  • 6/4In cases where anon-conforming productis detected, theRegulatory Authorityshallwithdraw the

concerned products from warehousesand take the necessarylegal actions.

  • 6/5Traffic departmentsshall verify theelectric vehicle registration documentsand itsdriving licensewhile

operating on public roads, in accordance with thetraffic regulations and proceduresin force.

  • 6/6Licensing authoritiesshall grantdriving licensesforelectric vehiclesonly after ensuring their compliance
with the requirements of this Regulation . Licenses shall be renewed upon confirming their safety during the
periodic inspection process , in accordance with the applicable regulations and procedures in Saudi Arabia .
Article (7): Responsibilities of Market Surveillance Authorities
Market Surveillance Authorities, as part of their competencies and powers , shall undertake the following:
  • 7/1Implementmarket surveillance proceduresfor products displayed in themarketsand products stored in
warehouses of traders and manufacturers to verify their safety and compliance with the essential
requirements set forth in this Regulation and relevant standards .
  • 7/2Withdrawsamples of the productfrom themarketorwarehouses of suppliers(manufacturers and
importers) to conduct necessary tests and verify their conformity with the requirements stated in this
Regulation .
11 Saudi Standards
www.saso.gov.sa
  • 7/3In cases where anon-conforming product—whether displayed or stored—is detected,Market
Surveillance Authorities shall take all necessary administrative measures regarding the concerned product.
The procedures and penalties outlined in Article (8) shall be applied after conducting the necessary legal
actions .
[Signature]
12 Saudi Standards
www.saso.gov.sa

Article (8): Violations and Penalties

  • 8/1It is prohibited tomanufacture, import, place, display, or even advertiseproducts thatdo not comply

with the provisions of thisRegulation.

  • 8/2Failure to meet therequirementsof thisRegulationshall be asufficient reasonforMarket Surveillance
Authorities and Regulatory Authorities to consider the product as non-conforming , as it may pose a risk to
consumer health, safety, and the environment , in the following cases:
o A) Failure to issue, or incorrect issuance of, the Certificate of Conformity or the Supplier Declaration of
Conformity .
o B) Unavailability or incompleteness of technical documentation (technical file, declaration of conformity...), or
the inclusion of incorrect or incomplete information .
  • 8/3In case of anyviolationof the provisions of thisRegulation,Market Surveillance Authoritiesshall—
depending on the case — take all necessary measures to eliminate the violation and its effects from the
market, including:
o A) Requiring the violating party — responsible for placing and displaying the non-conforming product — to
withdraw it from warehouses or the market in order to rectify the violation or export it , if possible, within
the timeframe specified by the Market Surveillance Authorities .
o B) Withdrawing, detaining, or taking any other necessary action to recall the product from the market. Market
Surveillance Authorities may, depending on the case, announce the withdrawal of the product from the
market, with the violating party bearing all associated expenses .
o C) Handling the non-conforming products covered by this Regulation in accordance with the laws and
regulations applicable to Regulatory Authorities and Market Surveillance Authorities .
  • 8/4In the event of aviolation involving electric vehicles,SASOshall take the necessarymeasuresagainst
non-conforming products , including the cancellation of the related Certificate of Conformity and taking the
necessary actions with the Notified (Approved) Body that issued the certificate, in accordance with the
Regulation of Conformity Assessment Bodies Acceptance .
  • 8/5Without prejudice to anyharsher penalties under applicable laws, any party thatviolates the
requirements of approved standards for products covered under this Regulation shall be subject to the
penalties stipulated in the Anti-Commercial Fraud Law .
[Signature]
13 Saudi Standards
www.saso.gov.sa

Article (9): General Provisions

  • 9/1Thesuppliershall bearfull legal responsibilityfor implementing therequirementsof thisRegulationand
shall be subject to penalties stipulated in the Anti-Commercial Fraud Law and/or any other related laws if
proven to have violated any provision of this Regulation .
  • 9/2ThisRegulationdoes not exempt thesupplierfrom complying withall other applicable laws and
regulations in Saudi Arabia , related to trading, transporting, and storing electric vehicles, as well as those
related to environmental, security, health, and safety standards.
  • 9/3Allsuppliers of electric vehiclessubject to thisRegulationmust provideRegulatory Inspectors and
Market Surveillance Authorities with all necessary facilities and information required for them to carry out
their assigned duties .
  • 9/4If anysituationarises thatcannot be addressedunder theprovisionsof thisRegulation, or ifany dispute
arises regarding its application , the matter shall be referred to a specialized committee within SASO , which
shall review the case and issue an appropriate decision , ensuring the public interest .
  • 9/5Thesuppliermay submit anew requestafter thereasonsfor the rejection of the initialconformity
assessment procedures request have been addressed. Necessary corrections must be made, and the supplier
shall bear any additional costs determined by SASO .
  • 9/6SASOshall reviewcomplaintsreceived regardingproducts with a Certificate of Conformity, verify the

validityof such complaints, and take the necessarylegal actionsin case of anyviolations.

  • 9/7SASOreserves the right torevoke the Certificate of Conformityif thesupplierviolates theprovisionsof

thisRegulation, and shall take necessarylegal measuresto safeguard itsrights.

  • 9/8Ifany modificationsare made to anelectric vehicleduring thevalidity periodof theCertificate of
Conformity or Registration Certificate ( except for cosmetic modifications that do not affect vehicle safety
or performance, as determined by SASO ), the certificate or Supplier Declaration of Conformity for the
product shall be revoked , and a new request must be submitted. Additionally, the supplier or authorized
representative must notify SASO — along with the Registration Certificate — when making any
modifications to the vehicle.
  • 9/9SASOshall have theexclusive righttointerpret the provisionsof thisRegulation, and all parties

benefiting from its applicationmust adhere to theinterpretations issued by SASO. [Signature]

14 Saudi Standards www.saso.gov.sa

Article (10): Transitional Provisions

  • 10/1The provisions of thisRegulationshall be enforced within a period not exceeding180 daysfrom the date

of its publication in theOfficial Gazette. [Signature]

  • 10/2Subject to the provisions ofClause (1)of thisArticle, suppliers shall be granted agrace periodto adjust
their market conditions in compliance with the requirements of this Technical Regulation , within a period not
exceeding 365 days from the date of its publication in the Official Gazette .
  • 10/3Upon adoption, thisRegulationshallsupersede all preceding regulationsin the field ofelectric vehicle

conformity assessment.

Article (11): Publication ThisRegulationshall be published in theOfficial Gazette. [Signature]

Annex (2): Essential Requirements for Electric Vehicles

  • Safety Requirements
The essential requirements aim to ensure safety aspects in electric vehicles and their components to minimize the
likelihood of accidents, fatalities, and electric shocks that may occur due to electric leakage from batteries or the
leakage of battery components into the passenger compartment .
1/1 Protection Against Electric Shocks
These electrical safety requirements apply to high-voltage connectors within the electrical system and electrical
components directly connected to it , provided they are not connected to high-voltage external power sources , in
accordance with the standards specified in Annex (1) .

To prevent direct contact , compliance with at least one of the following conditions must be verified:

passenger or luggage compartments .

removed in M3, M2, N3, and N2 vehicle categories , except by a qualified and certified person using the
necessary tools . However, connectors may be separated without tools if at least one of the following

  • C)Connectors must beequipped with a locking mechanism, requiringtwo separate actionsto disconnect

or, in M2, N2, N3, and M3 vehicle categories , by using an operator-controlled ON/OFF device or a similar
mechanism to disconnect the connector.
  • D)Thevoltage of conductive partsmust beequal to or less than 60V DC (V/AC) or less than 30V AC (V/DC)
